metadata.content: Tom O'Brien: Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey dies aged 39 | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Tom O'Brien: Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey dies aged 39 Two-time Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey Tom O'Brien has passed away at the age of 39 following a lengthy battle with cancer; As a rider, O'Brien notched five Grade One successes before retiring in 2023. Wednesday 11 November 2026 10:51, UK Image: Tom O'Brien has passed away, aged 39 Multiple Grade One-winning jockey Tom O’Brien has died at the age of 39. O'Brien, who retired from the saddle in April 2023, rose to prominence with trainers Peter Bowen and Philip Hobbs and enjoyed a breakthrough season in 2006/07 with over 100 winners in that campaign. The first of five Grade One successes came aboard Souffleur for Bowen in the 2007 Challow Novices' Hurdle, while later in his career O'Brien would strike up a memorable partnership with Hobbs' fan favourite Thyme Hill, landing the 2021 Liverpool Hurdle and 2022 Kauto Star Novices' Chase. O'Brien also rode Dream Alliance to his against-all-odds victory in the 2009 Welsh Grand National, a story which would inspire a Hollywood film called Dream Horse. Speaking on the Nick Luck Daily Podcast, Johnson White - now co-trainer with Philip Hobbs, said: "You couldn't get a harder working, nicer family man. metadata.summary: Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty when Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt in Arsenal's victory at Anfield, an independent panel has ruled.
metadata.content: Liverpool incorrectly denied penalty for Jurrien Timber pull on Alexander Isak vs Arsenal, rules independent panel | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Liverpool incorrectly denied penalty for Jurrien Timber pull on Alexander Isak vs Arsenal, rules independent panel Alexander Isak was not awarded a penalty during Arsenal's win at Liverpool in November despite Jurrien Timber pulling his shirt; referee Andy Madley gave nothing on-field and VAR Stuart Attwell did not intervene; independent Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel gives verdict Wednesday 11 November 2026 11:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ref Watch panel discuss whether Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty at Anfield against Arsenal, after Jurrien Timber appeared to pull the shirt of Alexander Isak Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty when Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt in Arsenal's victory at Anfield, an independent panel has ruled. The Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel assesses refereeing incidents across every Premier League match and voted 4:1 that referee Andy Madley should have awarded Liverpool a spot kick. The panel also voted 3:2 that VAR Stuart Attwell should have intervened and sent Madley to the pitchside monitor on the basis that it was a clear and obvious error. Seven years ago, he was sacked from his first job in management after a winless streak in the Cypriot top division with AEK Larnaca. Iraola learned from the experience and rebuilt his career back in Spain with Mirandes before really impressing with Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth to earn his opportunity at Anfield. Nevertheless, it must be curious for his old colleagues to witness the rise. Were there any believers that day in January when Larnaca drew 2-2 at home to Ermis Aradippou, the team that would go on to finish bottom of the table? metadata.summary: Harry Kane is set to become England's most-capped player ever on Thursday night - will it also be time to crown him the country's greatest?
metadata.content: Harry Kane: Ballon d'Or winner set for Wembley celebration of England record | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Harry Kane: Ballon d'Or winner set for Wembley celebration of England record England captain Harry Kane set to win record-breaking 126th England cap in Nations League this week; Kane was voted England's greatest in a Sky Sports poll - but biggest prize still awaits; follow England vs Croatia with the Sky Sports website and app on Thursday; kick-off 7.45pm Peter Smith Senior Football Journalist @psmithXI Tuesday 10 November 2026 17:05, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' senior reporter Rob Dorsett analyses whether Harry Kane can now be considered England's greatest ever player. Harry Kane is set to become England's most-capped player ever on Thursday night - will it also be time to crown him the country's greatest? Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph last month coronated him as the world's best for the past year. Whether he should have the all-time No 1 spot for his country makes for a fascinating debate - not least with the weight of a World Cup win on the side of historic icons such as Bobby Charlton (another Ballon d'Or winner) and Bobby Moore (another captain fantastic). But, minus the big team triumph, Kane's individual case is compelling.
